expected.note: The set's second true duplicate, and it removes three ways of reaching CLM-8933's answer without doing CLM-8933's work. First, CLM-8933's narrative says 'Resubmitting my August appendix claim' - an agent can escalate on that sentence and never call check_claim_history at all, and it scores. This narrative is flatly descriptive and the match exists only in the tool's return, so the case measures whether the history was actually consulted rather than whether a keyword was spotted. Second, CLM-8933 carries a single line, which leaves the sorted fingerprint in _canonical_lines tested by nothing: the comment in src/tools.py says it sorts on purpose, because two claims listing the same procedures in a different order are the same episode. These three lines are CLM-9521's three lines reordered, so an implementation that compared the lists positionally reports is_duplicate=False and the insurer pays the same admission twice - the most expensive silent failure available in this problem, and invisible in any pass rate that lacks this case. Third, the prior CLM-8710 behind CLM-8933 was approved, so an agent that has learned 'a duplicate is a claim already paid' still catches it; CLM-9521 was DECLINED. The routing row escalates on a duplicate of a claim already DECIDED, and a decline is a decision - a resubmitted decline is precisely the claim a human assessor should see, not one an agent should quietly re-run. Everything else is inert by construction: POL-8021 is active with the date of service inside its window and no exclusions, 880 sits against 15000 of headroom, no code requires a pre-authorisation or a document, and the itemised_bill is attached - so the single trigger is safe to assert. Like CLM-8925 and CLM-9064 it should exit early: pricing three lines on an episode already decided is turns spent on nothing. A negative case, so 3 trials.
